  <artifactId>demo-app</artifactId>

  <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <slf4j.version>2.0.18</slf4j.version>
  </properties>

  <dependencies>

    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
      <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
      <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
    </dependency>

      <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>

        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3.5.2</version>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

content.text:
Set up the Maven project at `nohook/`:

- **`pom.xml`** — `com.example:demo-app`, depends only on `org.slf4j:slf4j-api:2.0.18` (the facade, no binding attached), plus `junit-jupiter:6.1.3` for tests.
- **`src/main/java/com/example/App.java`** — uses `LoggerFactory.getLogger(App.class)` to log, with zero reference to any concrete implementation.
- **`src/test/java/com/example/AppTest.java`** — smoke test that `App.main` runs without throwing.
- **`.gitignore`** — ignores `target/`.

Verified with `mvn -o test` and `mvn -o compile exec:java` — both work. The `SLF4J(W): No SLF4J providers were found` warning is expected: only the facade is on the classpath, no binding. Whoever deploys this picks one (e.g. `logback-classic` or `log4j-slf4j2-impl`) and adds it as a separate dependency — that's the whole point of decoupling app code from the logging impl.
